My name is Anke. I grew up near Hamburg, and I have lived in Lisbon for six years. The first thing that confused me here was the weekend. In Germany, if you invite me to a barbecue on Saturday, I will write it down, and I will come. If it rains, we will have a fallback, usually somebody's garage. We almost never call things off at the last minute. Here, people say, if I have time, I will come, and I believed them. For months I waited for friends who were never going to arrive. Now I understand that a plan like that is tentative. It is not a promise. So I have changed too. I pencil things in, and I only commit to something when I really know. And if a Portuguese friend says maybe, I do not wait by the door any more. I bring a book.

I am Liam, and I come from a small town in Queensland. People from overseas think Australians never plan anything, and they are half right. On a Friday my friends and I will say, let's go fishing tomorrow, and then we play it by ear. If the weather looks iffy in the morning, we just stay home. Everything hinges on the sky. Last summer there was a massive downpour on the day of my brother's birthday, and half the guests took a rain check. Nobody was offended. That is the part visitors find strange. If you back out of a plan here, you say sorry, next time, and that is the end of it. My wife is German, and she still cannot believe it. She says, if you promise something, you do it. And to be honest, she has a point.
